### Question 1
```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
problem = pl.DataFrame({"values": [None, 18, 22, 45, 31, None, 85, 38, 129, 8001, 22, 3]}, strict = False)

mean_value = problem.select(pl.col('values').mean()).item()
filled_problem = problem.with_columns(pl.col('values').fill_null(mean_value).alias('values'))
standard_deviation = filled_problem.select(pl.col('values').std()).item()
print(mean_value)
print(round(standard_deviation, 2))
```


### Question 2

```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *
LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)
```

```{python}
df =pl.read_csv('names_year_csv.csv')
df.columns
df.head()
ann = (df.filter(pl.col("name") == "Ann")
    .select([
        "name",
        "year",
        "CO",
        "AR"
    ])
    .sort("year")
)


(
    (
    ggplot(ann, aes(x="year"))

    + geom_line(aes(y="CO"), color="orange", size=1)
    + geom_line(aes(y="AR"), color="blue", size=1)
    + geom_vline(xintercept=1968, color="black")
    # + annotate("text", x=1968, label="1968 Year", vjust=-1)
    + labs(
        title="The history of Ann for Colorado (orange) and Arizona (blue)",
        x="Year name given",
        y="Count of Ann"
    )
    + theme_light()
)
)
```


### Question 3
```{python}
import polars as pl

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn import metrics
```

```{python}
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4dwellings/master/data-raw/dwellings_ml/dwellings_ml.csv"
dwellings = pl.read_csv(url)
```


```{python}
dwellings = dwellings.with_columns(
    (pl.col("nocars") > 2)
    .cast(pl.Int64)
    .alias("many_cars")
)
```

```{python}
X = dwellings.drop([
    "parcel",
    "nocars",
    "many_cars"
])

y = dwellings.get_column("many_cars")

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X,
    y,
    test_size=0.30,
    random_state=2021
)


model = DecisionTreeClassifier(
    random_state=2021
)

model.fit(
    X_train,
    y_train
)


predictions = model.predict(
    X_test
)

accuracy = metrics.accuracy_score(
    y_test,
    predictions
)

print(round(accuracy, 2))

```

### Question 4
```{python}
import polars as pl
from lets_plot import *

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

url = (
    "http://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data_fivethirtyeight_starwars/master/survey_wide_all.csv"
)

starwars = pl.read_csv(url)


fan_starwars = (
    starwars
    .select([
        "gender",
        "fan_yn"
    ])
    .filter(
        pl.col("gender").is_not_null()
    )
    .with_columns(
        (
            pl.col("fan_yn")
            == "Yes"
        )
        .alias("a_fan")
    )
)

fan_proportion = (
    fan_starwars
    .group_by("gender")
    .agg(
        pl.col("a_fan")
        .mean()
        .alias("proportion")
    )
    .sort("gender")
)

print(
    fan_proportion.with_columns(
        pl.col("proportion").round(2)
    )
)
(
    ggplot(
        fan_proportion,
        aes(
            x="gender",
            y="proportion",
            fill="gender"
        )
    )
    + geom_bar(stat="identity")
    + labs(
        title="A real fan of Star Wars by Gender",
        x="Gender",
        y="Proportion",
        fill="Gender"
    )
    
    + theme_light()
)
```
